S22.01.needs: a web-grounded answer (the answer must come with sources; the chip only appears when the answer cites them)
S22.01.note: The chip text is the site host from the source data, so it is not a fixed label; the "+N" form uses the spCitationMore string. Whether a real answer returns cited sources depends on the server, which the code does not show.
steps: Open the side panel and ask a question that needs current web information, for example a news or price question.
Wait for the answer to finish streaming, then look inside the answer text for small chips where the source markers such as [1] would be.
Each chip shows the site host, or the host plus "+N" when sources are grouped. Click a chip with the mouse.
Compare: the source page should open in a new browser tab.
S22.01.where: Side panel > ask a question that needs web sources > read the answer text for small chips that show a site name (for example a host name with "+N" when several sources group)

S22.02.needs: a web-grounded answer with sources (a Mac trackpad or mouse is enough)
S22.02.note: The preview card has no fixed visible heading; its text comes from the source data. On desktop it opens on hover or keyboard focus, and touch opens it on the first tap.
steps: Use an answer that shows citation chips, as in S22.01.
Move the mouse pointer onto one chip and hold it there without clicking.
A card opens above or beside the chip, showing the source title, site host, and when present a snippet and a date.
Compare: the card should appear before any click, and a click on the chip should then open the source in a new tab.
S22.02.where: Side panel > the same web-grounded answer > move the mouse onto a citation chip (on a touch screen, tap it once)

S22.03.note: The footer list is for the answer's sources. Expanded agent steps show a separate list of titles with no snippet (under "Sources for $QUERY$" or similar); the code does not show the exact visible heading there.
steps: Ask a question that needs web sources and wait for the answer to finish.
Below the answer, find the line with the source count and click it to expand it.
The expanded list shows each source with its site host, title, and when present a snippet and date.
Click one source title; the page should open in a new browser tab.
S22.03.where: Side panel > the answer's sources line at the bottom of an answer (a line that reads like "3 sources")

labels.text: The map could not be loaded. You can still open these places in Maps.

S22.10.needs: a location question, and the map tiles must be configured for the app (the code stops with the unavailable message when they are not)
S22.10.note: Whether the map shows markers depends on the server sending a map-search card; the code only draws it when the server sends one, and it does not show whether tiles are configured in a given build. Pan and zoom controls were not verified in the code.
steps: Ask a location question such as a city or place name that the app can map.
Wait for the answer; a map search card appears under the answer text with its title and the place query.
Look for a map drawn under the title, with a marker for each place, and a list of the places below it.
Try to pan or zoom; if the map cannot load, the card shows the text "The map could not be loaded. You can still open these places in Maps." instead.
S22.10.where: Side panel > ask a location question (for example a place name) so the answer returns a map search card > the card shows a map with place markers under its title and a numbered list of places

labels.text: Your approval is required before this tool can run.

S22.28.needs: an agent run that pauses for approval (a tool that needs consent); a Free or paid account may matter, not verified in the code
S22.28.note: The approval block shows the "what will happen" details from the tool's inputs, and the "Allow for this chat" button is hidden for high-risk tools. The code does not show how the agent run is started from the first screen, so the start path is not confirmed. The old code reference bubbles.ts:493 no longer matches; the approval code is at apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts:954 to 1040.
steps: Start an agent task that will use a tool needing permission, for example one that changes something on the page.
When the run pauses, find the step row in the agent activity and click it to expand the details.
Read the approval block: it says "Your approval is required before this tool can run." (with a risk level in front when the tool has one) and lists what will happen.

Compare: Approve and Decline must both be visible, and a note field "Add guidance to steer the run (optional)" appears. Choose one and check the block changes to "Approved · decision recorded" or "Declined · decision recorded".
S22.28.where: Side panel > start an agent task that uses a tool needing approval > the step row in the agent activity > expand the step > the approval block with the buttons Approve, Allow for this chat and Decline
